newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan-Kuwait Bank H1 profits up 72 pct.
newsitem.headline: Jordan-Kuwait Bank H1 profits up 72 pct.

text.p: Jordan-Kuwait Bank said on Sunday said its pre-tax profits for the first half of 1996 rose to 2.3 million dinars ($3.24 million), up 72 percent against the same period last year.

A bank official told Reuters the jump was mainly credited to profits from the sale of some of the bank's stock portfolio and return on investment in Jordanian Brady bonds, which reached a total of 514,000 dinars.

Loans stood at 128.5 million dinars, a 9.7 percent rise in the first half of 1996 compared to the same period 1995. Deposits rose 8.1 percent to 222 million dinars during the first half of 1996 against the same period last year.

The bank's largest shareholders are Kuwaiti investors, including members of the ruling Sabah family, who hold 31 percent of its capital. The rest is held by Jordanian investors. Its assets rose six percent in the first half of 1996 to 263.7 million dinars.
The bank wants to double its capital to 20 million dinars from its reserves by 1997 in line with Central Bank rules.
Shareholders' rights -- capital and reserves -- stood at 19.2 million dinars in the first half of 1996, the bank said.
